hook_text: Mbombela gets around eight hundred millimetres of rain a year. Port Nolloth gets well under one hundred. Same country, so why?
clip_script: Two schools, two rain gauges. In Mbombela, summer storms fill the gauge again and again. In Port Nolloth, the gauge stays almost empty, and fog rolls in from a cold sea instead. On the world rainfall map, the wettest places hug the equator, where hot air rises and makes rain. The driest places lie near the tropics, where dry air sinks. Mountains, the sea and ocean currents add their own twists.
visual_style: Whiteboard world map shaded dark blue at the equator and pale yellow near the tropics, with arrows of rising and sinking air, and a mountain with clouds on one side and dry land on the other.
mood: Curious and clear, like solving a puzzle.
pacing: Two quick gauge readings, then step by step through the map and the reasons.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the wettest and driest places on a world rainfall map in your atlas.
